newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary APV offers shares for coupons in Forte.
newsitem.headline: Hungary APV offers shares for coupons in Forte.

text.p: Hungary's state privatisation agency APV Rt will offer a 45.6-percent stake in photographic products company Forte Fotokemia Rt against compensation coupons, officials involved in the transaction said.

The stake represents 491,179 shares of 1,000 forints ($5.21) face value, with allocation preference to be given to original coupon holders and employees, Tibor Tamas, Deputy General Director of lead manager Postabank Securities said on Monday.
"Of course, preference for these two groups of investors does not mean that only these two groups are entitled to subscribe," Tamas said.
Subscriptions will run from July 21 to August 1, and investors will have to pay two 1,000-forint coupons for every five Forte shares.

Compensation coupons are securities awarded to victims of Hungary's fascist and communist regimes. The coupons have a lively secondary market on the Budapest Stock Exchange, where they closed at 810 forints, down five, on Monday.
Gyorgy Pinke, head of APV's Capital Market and Property Transfer Managing Directorate, said the swap ratio reflects the low profitability of Forte.

"This plant has a very stable performance. It is a stable investment on the long-term, but we have to say that based on its current profitability, it does not belong among the best (companies)," Pinke said.
In 1996, Forte had a slim after-tax profit of 1.3 million forints on net sales of 1.76 billion forints.
In the first three months of 1997, it had a preliminary operating loss of 8.2 million forints compared to an operating loss of 33.1 million in all of 1996.

Tamas said the company's shareholder structure and APV's offering a minority stake were factors in setting the swap ratio. The organisation of Employee Share Option Programme has a majority holding in Forte.
The Forte transaction is part of APV's plan to maintain a continuous supply of state assets against coupons.

"APV is determined...to continuously offer assets through the whole year for compensation coupons," Pinke said. "We have just completed a (similar) transaction in (dairy firm) Szabolcstej, and a share-for-coupon swap in Forte is the next step."

Pinke said APV will continue share-for-coupon swaps in the autumn when it offers a share package worth more than two billion forints in Budapesti Ingatlan Hasznositasi es Fejlesztesi Rt, a property management company to be listed on the Budapest Stock Exchange.
Later this year, APV also plans to offer stakes for coupons in two electricity distributors, Pinke said. Stakes in another four such firms would be available next year.

APV is looking to sell stakes worth six to eight percent of the issued share capital in five of the country's six regional electricity distributors. A smaller stake would be offered in the sixth, Elmu Rt.
